sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: The Art of the Umayyad Period in Spain
sources.note: Institutional chronology: emirate 756 to 929; caliphate from 929. Does not certify polygons.

sources.title: Mosque-Cathedral: Original Mosque of Abd al-Rahman I
sources.note: Building description: eleven naves, superimposed arches, reused materials, mortar floor and wooden roof.

sources.title: María Teresa Casal García: El arrabal de Šaqunda, un modelo temprano de urbanismo omeya
sources.note: University of Alicante research abstract: planned streets, commercial and productive buildings, 818 suppression.

sources.title: María Teresa Casal García: The Rabad of Saqunda in Umayyad Cordoba, 2018
sources.note: Author-uploaded chapter, pages 119 to 132, full text read. Wells pp124 to125; courtyards and absence of dedicated latrine rooms pp126 to127.

sources.title: Casal, Martínez and Araque: Estudio de los vertederos domésticos del arrabal de Saqunda, 2009 to 2010
sources.note: Author-uploaded full article, pp143 to182; pottery p152; worked bovine scapulae pp173 to178. Their learning function is an interpretation.

sources.title: Piñero Palacios and Rodríguez Pérez: Nuevas aportaciones sobre el arrabal emiral de Saqunda, 2019
sources.note: Full PDF downloaded from journal /article/download/12446/11125. Printed p377 figure10 visually inspected, local PDF index30. Only surviving الرحمن الرحيم quoted, not bracketed reconstruction. P376 cursive and incision; p380 dating.

sources.title: Historical Dictionary of Switzerland: Second kingdom of Burgundy
sources.note: Rudolfian kingdom 888 to1032, Rhône expansion, distinction from Dijon duchy; incorporation into Empire1032to1038.

sources.title: Department of Isère: Les fouilles archéologiques du site de Colletière
sources.note: Settlement, food, crafts and music. Gives1006to1040; earlier research gives1003to1034, so public text uses early11thcentury.

sources.title: Paladru Archaeological Museum: Dans les pas des artisans de l’an Mil
sources.note: Child shoe, maple last, leather offcuts, oak templates, awls and varied stitching. Museum imagined play scene not treated as evidence.

sources.title: Payerne Abbey: Histoire et patrimoine
sources.note: Royal Burgundian patronage, Adelaide and Cluny,11thcenturyRomanesque church.

sources.title: Historical Dictionary of Switzerland: Hospice du Grand-Saint-Bernard
sources.note: Attested1125; traditional1050foundation uncertain; pilgrim assistance,78dependencies1177. Rescue dogs only attestedlate17thcentury, not used as medieval detail.

sources.title: Neuchâtel Historical and Archaeological Society: La première mention écrite de Neuchâtel
sources.note: Vincent Callet-Molin;24April1011charter, ArchivesIsère1G11, Latin phrases transcribed in Description, seal and unfree estate labourers.

sources.title: Philippe Lanoë: La frontière orientale de la Bretagne
sources.note: Bretagne Culture Diversité: ninth-century expansion, Viking disruption, duchy,1532union.

sources.title: Inrap annual report 2023: Vannes renoue avec les ducs de Bretagne
sources.note: Indexed full excavation account pp46to47: château de l’Hermine built1380, latrines,mill,objects. Avoid first-evermill claim.

sources.title: Inrap: Des pots pour les habitants de Rennes
sources.note: Medieval pottery production atChartres-de-Bretagne, late10thto13thcenturies; householdforms and productionwasters.

sources.title: Laurence Moal: Réceptions et banquets dans le duché de Bretagne au XVe siècle
sources.note: Historian drawing on Rennes municipal accounts;1475embassy expenses,banquetfood,breadplates. Elite diplomatic events,notordinarydiet.

sources.title: Bibliothèque nationale de France: Le catholicon en troys langaiges
sources.note: Catalogue transcribes historical French title, Tréguier 5 November 1499, JeanCalvez; language learning dictionaryBretonFrenchLatin.

sources.title: Bretagne Culture Diversité: Au bout du monde, au cœur des échanges
sources.note: Fifteenth-century linenexports and Castilian merchants inNantes;latercolonialtradeexcluded.

sources.title: Patrick Galliou: L’arrivée des Bretons en Armorique
sources.note: Historian’s assessment of migration evidence, sixth-century councils and disputed scale of settlement.

sources.title: Institut culturel de Bretagne: Vannes, comté de, ou Broérec
sources.note: Indexed full entry: Vannes region between Ellé and Vilaine, Carolingian march, eventual incorporation into the duchy. Its problematic early ruler dates are not adopted.

sources.title: Inrap: Un habitat de l’âge du Bronze et une ferme médiévale découverts à Caudan
sources.note: Medieval captions explicitly date enclosure, drying pits, storage silo and sill-built structure to sixth through ninth centuries. Bronze Age finds excluded.

sources.title: Musée de l’ancienne abbaye de Landévennec: Site et musée
sources.note: Indexed museum account: earliest oratory/cemetery, later ninth-century monastic buildings and book copying.

sources.title: CNRS IKER Arbres: Vieux breton, vieux brittonique
sources.note: Syntax section cites Lambert 2011 for nimer, constellation, in Angers 477 folio 14b. Distinguishes disputed phrase interpretations and modern language classifications.

sources.title: Jacopo Bisagni: Angers BM MS 477, Breton Handlist
sources.note: University of Galway catalogue: second unit dated 897, numerous Old Breton glosses, Breton scribes but disputed place of production.

sources.title: Han Nijdam and Otto S. Knottnerus: Redbad, Fryslân 24/6, 2018
sources.note: Printed page 14: marriage alliance, Redbad’s death in 719, gradual Frankish conquest in 734 and late eighth century.

sources.title: University of Groningen: Settlement development of Frisian terp sites
sources.note: Long-term mound development and building materials, from Iron Age to later Middle Ages. Avoid claiming uninterrupted ethnic identity from Roman Frisii.

sources.title: Fries Museum: The fibula from Wijnaldum
sources.note: Seventh-century brooch; over 300 garnets, likely Indian origin, elite female wearer interpretation. Museum Dutch page currently dates around 600 rather than English page 625; public text uses early seventh century.

sources.title: Rijksmuseum van Oudheden: Dorestad, wereldstad in de middeleeuwen
sources.note: International Rhine market around 800, shipping and craft workers. Broader North Sea/Frankish trade context, not independent Frisian rule at that date.

sources.title: Ewiges Meer heritage route: Bernuthsfeld
sources.note: Heritage interpretation in cooperation with Landesmuseum Emden: wool garment assembled from 45 reused textile pieces, preservation and CT examination.

sources.title: Ostfriesische Landschaft annual report 2024
sources.note: Research project section places Bernuthsfeld clothing around AD 700.

sources.title: RuneS Academy database: Oostum comb, find 703
sources.note: Antler comb, 700 to 950, fuþorc inscription. Published transliteration includes cabu and dedahabucu. Interpretations disagree about whether Habuku made it for Aib or Aib for Habuku. Short cabu only, clearly transliteration.

sources.title: University of Groningen: Two thousand years of horse beans on the salt marshes
sources.note: Archaeobotanist Mans Schepers on long-term barley/bean cultivation and modern experimental plots; modern trial results not presented as measured medieval yields.

sources.title: Ernst Schubert: Die Sachsen im Frühmittelalter, Portal Niedersachsen
sources.note: Social distinctions, loose political organisation, conquest and elite integration. Avoid obsolete assertions of virtually absent transport or deterministic ethnic origins.

sources.title: Niedersächsische Landeszentrale für politische Bildung: Niedersachsen, ein Porträt
sources.note: Historical chronology: Saxon wars 772 to 804 and incorporation into Frankish realm.

sources.title: LWL Westfälische Geschichte: Sächsische Siedlung bei Warendorf, model and archaeological interpretation
sources.note: Excavated seventh/eighth-century farm plans, rebuilding, sunken workshops and river crossing. Specific conjectural functions labelled; exact settlement foundation and end dates omitted because institutional accounts differ.

sources.title: Ingo Pfeffer and Dennis Becker, LWL: Nichts als Grubenhäuser?
sources.note: Indexed full 2022 excavation report: early medieval Milte, burned loom, seven complete and twelve fragmentary weights, exact loom date not yet stated.

sources.title: Wilhelm Winkelmann: Beiträge zur Frühgeschichte Westfalens
sources.note: Indexed text of Warendorf settlement discussion: bowls, rounded pots, pierced suspension holes, local wares and Rhineland imports, later seventh century to around 800.

sources.title: University of Notre Dame: Hêliand 56, text and translation by Jake Coen
sources.note: Section 56, lines 4665 to 4701, text transcribed from Vanneufville 2008. Short gesidos mine quote and translation my companions; modern scholarly edition of attested Old Saxon in Latin letters.

sources.title: Nelson Goering: Heliand lines 503b to 535a in three manuscripts, Ghent University
sources.note: Introduction page 1: poem first half ninth century, Munich manuscript around or shortly after 850; Latin-letter manuscript tradition.

sources.title: Michel Zimmermann: L’Espagne wisigothique
sources.note: Overview by emeritus medieval-history professor; used for broad movement, Toulouse/Toledo phases and 711 conquest, not older essentialist ethnic characterisations or detailed conquest legends.

sources.title: Inrap: Les Goths à Toulouse, 413 to 508
sources.note: Probable palace, civic-religious ensemble, dress objects and mixed burial grounds. Architectural identifications remain qualified.

sources.title: Musée Saint-Raymond / Ministry of Culture: bone comb, Joconde 05630030006
sources.note: Museum-authored 2020 exhibition label: single-row bone combs from southwestern Gaul, rounded backs and dotted-circle decoration, parallels with Chernyakhov culture.

sources.title: Castilla-La Mancha archaeological park: Recópolis site guide
sources.note: Indexed guide, commercial workshops and page 11 housing/water. Use excavated domestic and production evidence, not the debated 1945 coin-hoard discovery. Site identification conventional and stated as such.

sources.title: Museo Nacional de Arte Romano: Época visigoda
sources.note: Indexed full museum account: late-antique Mérida, decorative sculpture, funerary inscriptions, pottery and sixth-century mosaic continuity.

sources.title: Molina Gómez and Zapata Parra: El hallazgo de un tremis de Recaredo I en Begastri
sources.note: University of Murcia repository, Antigüedad y Cristianismo XXV pp.265 to 268; coin MC-824, reign 586 to 601, Latin legend REX, TOLETO, PIVS; weight 1.480 g and diameter 18 mm.
